description.narrative:
The Altruistech Skills-To-Job Program bridges the gap between graduation and employment for recent graduates in Sierra Leone. The program equips recent graduates, especially women with practical workplace, digital, and professional skills required to succeed in both online (remote) and on-site(corporate, NGO, SME) work environments.
We will be establishing a maker space where they learn Robotics <(>&<)> IoT Engineering, Research <(>&<)> Data Analytics, Product Development, AI and Software Development, Social Media <(>&<)> content creation, Entrepreneurship and start-up development.
Upon successful completion of the training phase, participants receive a Corporate Workplace Readiness Certificate, followed by a 3-month stipend-based internship at Altruistech Luminary Center, to enhance their working experience, and through our partners, we provide job placement opportunities, either online or on-site, based onindividual performance, employer demand, and participant preference.
Our overall goal is to prepare recentgraduates for immediate employment by equipping them with practical skills, real-world experience, and direct pathways into work and entrepreneurship. Our objective is to bridge the gap between individual capabilities and employer needs, by creating a skilled, employable workforce through training in high-demand technical (hard) skills and crucial workplace(soft/employability) skills.
Our key activities include expanding the capacity of our current maker space, executing marketing activities to recruitstudents, increasing our partnership efforts, conducting a 6-month per cohort training and internship for our students and project closure.

participating-org.narrative:
Altruistech Luminary Center is a social enterprise focusing on providing equal access to STEAM education and economic opportunitiesfor children and youths in Sierra Leone. We envision becoming the leading creative technology and work readiness skills developmenthub in Sierra Leone.
For the youths and recent graduates, our objective is to provide online and on-site work readiness skills for5000 recent graduates in Sierra Leone in 5 years through the development of a maker space that trains young people on in-demand workand entrepreneurial skills.
Our overall mission is to empower young people in Africa with the tools, knowledge, and skills they need to acquire jobs, become innovators, problem solvers, and champions of sustainable development. Thus, we are building a creative maker space where they learn Robotics <(>&<)> IoT Engineering, Research <(>&<)> Data Analytics, Product Development, AI and Software Development, Social Media <(>&<)> content creation,Entrepreneurship and start-up development.
Our focus is mainly on on recent graduates between the ages of 18 and 35 years old including women and people living with disabilities in Sierra Leone.
